Selection and update policy for per-CPU stat thresholds and small-counter overflow handling.
Behaviour of generic modification, combined fold, high pageset decay, zone drain, and online-iteration helpers referenced but not routed.

findings.text: Provides a per-zone reclaim pressure limit derived from the gap between low and minimum watermarks scaled down by the number of online processors. Callers use it as a conservative trigger that stays safely above the minimum reserve despite stale estimates.
The derived pressure limit never falls below one page and never exceeds a fixed upper bound, so small watermark gaps still yield progress and very large gaps do not delay reclaim excessively.

Global counters can lag per-CPU batches, so an apparently healthy estimate may mask a real minimum breach on machines with high limits or many processors. The pressure limit is intentionally reduced to absorb worst-case drift.
Offers per-node counter adjustment through a small per-CPU delta that is folded into the node global counter only after crossing a per-CPU threshold, reducing contention on frequent updates.

On a threshold crossing the per-CPU delta is not cleared to zero but left with an opposite-polarity bias equal to half the threshold, creating hysteresis that avoids immediate refolding on the next update.
Page-addressed helpers resolve the owning node or zone from the page and then apply the corresponding node or zone adjustment, so callers account memory events without tracking topology themselves.
One build variant of the public increment and decrement helpers delegates to a generic node modification path with unit deltas, centralizing threshold and overflow policy outside the wrappers.

An alternate build variant protects the internal adjustment with local interrupt masking around the per-CPU update, making the increment and decrement safe against interrupt-context races on that processor.

Internal per-node adjustments run with nested preemption disabled across the per-CPU read-modify-write and conditional global fold, preserving the association between delta and threshold on the current processor.

Folds the current processor pending zone and node deltas into global counters and optionally performs pageset maintenance, reporting whether any counter change, high-watermark decay, or drain activity occurred.

Zone deltas are exchanged to zero and added to per-zone globals only when nonzero, with matching aggregates kept for a later combined fold. Node deltas follow the same exchange-and-add pattern over all online nodes.

Remote pageset maintenance has armed, exempt, waiting, and drained outcomes keyed by locality, residual count, and an idle counter. Activity rearms the counter, node-local zones stay exempt, nonzero counters keep waiting, and expiry with residual pages causes a drain.
Reports a node-wide total for one NUMA event by summing that event value across every zone slot belonging to the node.
Groups three unsigned totals describing contiguous allocation health: currently free pages, total free blocks, and the subset of free blocks considered suitable.
Two system-wide atomic long counters track total pages occupied by the memory map and the subset allocated during boot, providing stable counters for diagnostics and sizing.

Exposes a single indexed string table mapping each statistics enumeration to its reporting name, partitioned into zone items, NUMA events, node items, system-wide items, and conditional event items, with selected events expanded once per zone kind.

Zone-qualified event names are generated per memory-zone kind with compile-time selection. Unavailable zone kinds contribute no entries while normal and movable always contribute, keeping indices aligned with enabled configuration.
Implements position-based iteration over online memory nodes for reporting, where start seeks to the requested node offset, next advances to the following online node, and stop performs no cleanup.
Central zone walker visits every zone slot of a node, optionally skipping unpopulated zones and optionally holding each zone interrupt-protected spinlock only around the per-zone print callback.

Fragmentation reporting prints one line per populated zone with free counts by page order. Extended page-type reporting adds a header plus per-migratetype free counts by order and a separate per-migratetype block-count summary.
Free-list accounting temporarily releases the zone lock around a scheduling point once per page order while scanning, then reacquires it before continuing, bounding uninterrupted lock hold time.

Because free lists can be very long, displayed free counts stop after a large fixed number of entries and flag overflow, trading exactness for avoidance of lockup-detector triggers while holding a spinlock for diagnostics.
Per-order free counters used by the basic fragmentation line are read without synchronization for display only and may race with allocators. They must not drive allocation or reclaim decisions.
Block-type census steps through the zone by pageblock stride, ignores holes without online pages and pages owned by another zone, and tallies only migrate types within the known range.

Fixed numeric policy values observed are a minimum pressure result of 1, a maximum pressure result of 125, a remote pageset idle delay initialized to 3 after activity, and a diagnostic free-list display cap of 100000 entries.
